children.title: Observer States as Information Gain Processes

detail.title: Observer States as Information Gain Processes
detail.summary: Observation in both physical systems and computer networks can be modeled as a formal measurement process that resolves uncertainty, functioning as an information-gain mechanism.
detail.reason: This notebook synthesizes the existing evidence for proj-observer-001, transitioning the project from initial inquiry to a established finding.

detail.title: Observer Interaction and Informational Entropy
detail.summary: This synthesis explores the duality of measurement: whether it acts as a physical perturbation or an acquisition of informational state. By drawing on network analysis and quantum theory, we propose that the 'observer effect' is not a singular phenomenon but a spectrum of system coupling.
detail.reason: This notebook establishes a baseline for the reactivated observer project using available collected evidence.

detail.title: Observer Perturbation vs. Informational Entropy
detail.summary: A framework distinguishing measurement-based perturbation (physical change) from informational entropy (state knowledge), supported by algorithmic information theory.
detail.reason: Synthesis of evidence into a provisional framework to advance the observer-effect research project.
